beats.title: Washington Sworn In as President
beats.description: On a balcony in New York, a Revolutionary War general took the oath to lead the new republic under its young Constitution.

beats.title: John Adams Becomes President
beats.description: The nation's first vice president took the oath in Philadelphia, succeeding the man who had stepped down after two terms.

beats.title: Jefferson Takes the Oath
beats.description: The first president inaugurated in the new capital city, Washington, followed a bitterly contested election decided in the House.

beats.title: James Madison Takes Office
beats.description: The principal author of the Constitution became the fourth president, wearing a suit of American-made wool at his ceremony.

beats.title: James Monroe Inaugurated Outdoors
beats.description: The ceremony moved outside to a platform in front of Congress because of a dispute over seating, launching an era of good feelings.

beats.title: John Quincy Adams Takes Office
beats.description: The son of a former president was sworn in after the House settled an election in which no candidate had a majority.

beats.title: Andrew Jackson Inaugurated
beats.description: A frontier general's swearing-in drew a huge crowd that mobbed the White House reception, wrecking furniture and china.

beats.title: Martin Van Buren Sworn In
beats.description: Jackson's chosen successor, the first president born a US citizen rather than a British subject, took the oath at the Capitol.

beats.title: William Henry Harrison Inaugurated
beats.description: He gave the longest inaugural speech in history in freezing weather, then died of illness barely a month into his term.

beats.title: James K. Polk Takes Office
beats.description: The first so-called dark horse nominee was sworn in on a rainy day, and his ceremony was among the first reported by telegraph.

beats.title: Zachary Taylor Becomes President
beats.description: A war hero who had never voted took office, a day later than planned because the traditional date fell on a Sunday.
beats.note: Oath taken March 5, the day after the term began.

beats.title: Franklin Pierce Takes the Oath
beats.description: A New Hampshire Democrat affirmed rather than swore his oath, weeks after losing his young son in a railway accident.

beats.title: James Buchanan Inaugurated
beats.description: The only bachelor president took office as slavery tensions mounted, and a Supreme Court ruling on it followed days later.

beats.title: Lincoln Sworn In as President
beats.description: Guarded by soldiers, a lawyer from Illinois pleaded with seceding states in his speech as the nation edged towards war.

beats.title: Andrew Johnson Takes Office
beats.description: A vice president sworn in at a hotel after the sudden assassination of his predecessor became the 17th president.
beats.note: Succeeded on Lincoln's death; first oath, April 15.

beats.title: Ulysses S. Grant Inaugurated
beats.description: The victorious Union general became president, and his predecessor refused to attend the ceremony.

beats.title: Rutherford B. Hayes Takes Oath
beats.description: After a deadlocked contest settled by a special commission, he swore the oath privately first, as the formal day fell on a Sunday.
beats.note: Private oath March 3, public oath March 5; same year.

beats.title: James Garfield Inaugurated
beats.description: A former Civil War general and Ohio congressman took the oath, and was shot by an assassin only months afterward.

beats.title: Grover Cleveland Takes Office
beats.description: The first Democrat in the White House since before the Civil War was sworn in, a bachelor who later married in the mansion.
beats.note: First inauguration of two non-consecutive terms.

beats.title: Benjamin Harrison Sworn In
beats.description: The grandson of a former president took office in pouring rain, having won the electoral vote while losing the popular one.

beats.title: William McKinley Inaugurated
beats.description: The Ohio Republican took office in a ceremony that was among the first to be captured by a motion picture camera.

beats.title: Theodore Roosevelt Sworn In
beats.description: At 42, the youngest man ever to hold the office took the oath in a Buffalo home after an assassin's bullet killed his predecessor.
beats.note: Succeeded on McKinley's death; first oath, September 14.

beats.title: William Howard Taft Takes Office
beats.description: A snowstorm forced the ceremony indoors for the future chief justice, the heaviest man to ever hold the presidency.

beats.title: Woodrow Wilson Inaugurated
beats.description: A former Princeton professor and governor became the first Democratic president in sixteen years, and a suffrage march filled the streets.

beats.title: Warren G. Harding Takes Office
beats.description: The first inauguration to feature a loudspeaker system carried the Ohio Republican's promise of a return to normalcy.

beats.title: Coolidge Sworn In by Lamplight
beats.description: In a Vermont farmhouse, his own father, a local official, administered the oath after the sudden death of the president in office.
beats.note: Succeeded on Harding's death; first oath, August 3.

beats.title: Herbert Hoover Inaugurated
beats.description: A celebrated engineer and relief organiser took office promising prosperity just months before the stock market collapsed.

beats.title: Franklin Roosevelt Takes Office
beats.description: In the depths of the Depression, he told the nation the only thing to fear was fear itself.

beats.title: Truman Sworn In After Roosevelt
beats.description: A Missouri senator and vice president took the oath within hours of his predecessor's death, with the war still raging.
beats.note: Succeeded on Roosevelt's death; first oath, April 12.

beats.title: Eisenhower Takes Office
beats.description: The wartime Supreme Allied Commander opened his term with a prayer he had composed himself, the first Republican victory in decades.

beats.title: Kennedy Inaugurated in the Snow
beats.description: The youngest elected president urged Americans to ask what they could do for their country, on a bright, bitterly cold day.

beats.title: LBJ Sworn In on Air Force One
beats.description: A Texan took the oath aboard a parked aircraft, with the widow of the slain president standing at his side.
beats.note: Succeeded on Kennedy's death; first oath, November 22.

beats.title: Richard Nixon Takes Office
beats.description: A California Republican who had narrowly lost eight years earlier was sworn in amid deep divisions over a distant war.

beats.title: Gerald Ford Sworn In
beats.description: The only president never elected to either office declared that the long national nightmare was over after his predecessor resigned.

beats.title: Jimmy Carter Inaugurated
beats.description: A Georgia peanut farmer and former governor walked much of the parade route to the White House rather than ride.

beats.title: Reagan Takes the Oath
beats.description: A former actor and governor became the oldest man yet elected, and the American hostages in Tehran were freed that same day.

beats.title: George H. W. Bush Inaugurated
beats.description: The sitting vice president and former CIA director took office, promising a kinder, gentler nation.

beats.title: Bill Clinton Takes Office
beats.description: A young Arkansas governor became the first baby boomer president, in a ceremony featuring a poem by Maya Angelou.

beats.title: George W. Bush Sworn In
beats.description: The son of a former president took office after a razor-thin contest was settled by the Supreme Court and a Florida recount.

beats.title: Barack Obama Inaugurated
beats.description: The first Black president took the oath before an enormous crowd on the National Mall amid a deep financial crisis.
